content:
Data handling is the child's first taste of reading information — counting pictures in a graph, reading a small table, comparing groups. It rewards careful counting over cleverness. Here is what the Olympiad tests, the facts to hold on to, the slips to avoid, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 1 Data Handling Olympiad tests

  • Reading a picture graph (pictograph) and counting objects
  • Reading a simple table
  • Finding which group has the most or the fewest
  • Working out how many more one group has, and the total of all groups

Key facts your child should know

  • In a picture graph, each picture stands for a count — read a row by counting its pictures.
  • Most means the largest number; fewest means the smallest.
  • "How many more" between two rows is a subtraction.
  • The total is the sum of every row.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Miscounting the pictures in a row by one.
  • Adding two rows when the question asks how many more (a subtraction).
  • Reading "fewest" as "most".

quiz.title: IMO Class 1 Data Handling Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: In a picture graph, 1 picture stands for 2 kites. Sara's row has 7 pictures. How many kites does Sara have?
questions.explanation: Each picture means 2 kites. So 7 pictures show 7 × 2 = 14 kites.

questions.q: In a picture graph, 1 picture stands for 2 toy trains. Veer's row has 3 pictures. How many toy trains does Veer have?
questions.explanation: Each picture means 2 toy trains. So 3 pictures show 3 × 2 = 6 toy trains.

questions.q: Children chose a favourite fruit: 12 chose mango, 9 chose apple, 6 chose grapes, 4 chose banana. Which two choices together were made by exactly 18 children?
In a picture graph, 1 picture stands for 2 balloons. Riya's row has 6 pictures. How many balloons does Riya have?
questions.explanation: Each picture means 2 balloons. So 6 pictures show 6 × 2 = 12 balloons.

questions.q: In a picture graph, 1 picture stands for 2 toffees. How many pictures are needed to show 10 toffees?
questions.explanation: Put the toffees in pairs: 10 makes 5 pairs, so 5 pictures are needed.

questions.q: The table shows stars earned: Wed 6, Thu 11, Fri 8. How many more stars earned on Thu than on Wed?
In a class survey about a favourite game, 9 children chose cricket, 8 chose hide-and-seek and 3 chose hopscotch. How many children were asked in all?
In a survey about a favourite toy, 5 children like teddy bear, 10 like toy train and 7 like kite. How many more children like toy train than teddy bear?
questions.explanation: Take away: 10 − 5 = 5 more children like toy train.

questions.q: A pet shop has 4 puppies, 6 kittens and 3 rabbits. How many animals are there in all?
Children chose a favourite pet: 14 chose dog, 9 chose cat, 5 chose fish, 2 chose parrot. Which two choices together were made by exactly 14 children?

faq.a: A picture graph where each picture represents a number of things, so you count the pictures to read the data.

faq.q: How do you find "how many more"?
faq.a: Subtract the smaller count from the larger one.
